## Physical scenario

A monatomic ideal gas is taken around the cycle shown in figure in the direction shown in the figure. The path for process $c \rightarrow a$ is a straight line in the $pV$-diagram.

## Question

What is the efficiency of the cycle?

## Answer choices

- A: A: 10\%

- B: B: 11.1\%

- C: C: 15.9\%

- D: D: 12.3\%

## Figure caption (auxiliary; use the image as primary evidence)

The image is a pressure-volume (P-V) diagram of a thermodynamic process. It features the following components:

- **Axes**: 
  - The vertical axis is labeled “\(p\)” for pressure, with markings at \(1.00 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa}\) and \(3.00 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa}\).
  - The horizontal axis is labeled “\(V\)” for volume, with markings at \(0.500\, \text{m}^3\) and \(0.800\, \text{m}^3\).

- **Points**:
  - Point \(a\) is at the coordinate \((0.500\, \text{m}^3, 3.00 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa})\).
  - Point \(b\) is at \((0.800\, \text{m}^3, 3.00 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa})\).
  - Point \(c\) is at \((0.800\, \text{m}^3, 1.00 \times 10^5 \, \text{Pa})\).

- **Process Arrows**:
  - An arrow from \(a\) to \(b\) indicates an isobaric expansion.
  - An arrow from \(b\) to \(c\) indicates an isochoric decrease in pressure.
  - An arrow from \(c\) to \(a\) indicates an isochoric increase in pressure, completing a cyclic process.

The diagram depicts a cycle involving processes at constant pressure and constant volume.
